title: Dimension reduction in L_p
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that for every fixed 1 < p < infinity, p != 2, and distortion D > 1, every n points of an L_p space embed into l_p^d with distortion at most D for d = exp(O((log n)^gamma)), gamma = 2-p below 2 and 1-2/p above 2, so d = n^o(1), while exact embeddings need about n^2/16 coordinates. The first lesson proves the convexity tools, Ball's exact bound, the counting lower bound and the quadratic lower bound for exact embeddings. The second reduces the upper bound, by convex separation and Maurey's sampling, to one random normalized gradient with nearly equal weighted moments. The third bounds the absolute row sums of a reweighted projection onto normalized gradients through the localization of electrical flows. The fourth builds the gradient for 1 < p < 2 from a stable-type Poisson sum, and the fifth for p > 2 from overlapping truncations and Poisson sampling with nearly additive moments.
